archetype.name: Gunslinger (downfield-first)
archetype.definition: A pocket thrower who wins by pushing the ball 10-plus yards into tight windows and accepts interceptions as the price, now leaning on that downfield game more than at any point in his last two good seasons.

report.headline: Deep ball still works; everything short of the sticks is broken
report.take:
Darnold arrived at this season off two strong years. In 2025 he posted 8.49 yards per attempt, a +5.2 CPOE and 0.162 EPA per play, ranked 14th. This year he has fallen to -0.046 EPA per dropback (33rd of 54), a -2.01 CPOE and a 4.3% interception rate that ranks 46th. The surface reading is that the old Jets-era Darnold is back. The splits say something narrower and more interesting. He has been very good throwing downfield and poor throwing short.

On throws of 10-plus air yards he is at 0.398 EPA per attempt with a +3.6 CPOE. His 20 deep attempts have produced 19.3 EPA, a 15.3 CPOE and no picks. Under 10 air yards the same passer sits at -0.142 EPA, a -5.5 CPOE and six interceptions. Throws behind the line alone have cost 16.2 points. The middle of the field has given him no touchdowns and three interceptions. His aggressiveness is up 5.5 points on last year and his time to throw is up too. That fits a quarterback who is hunting the shot because the quick game isn't paying.

The quick game isn't paying largely because of protection and the supporting cast. He has been pressured on 30.7% of dropbacks, 41st of 42, and Seattle's offensive hit rate ranks 28th. Yet his pressure-to-sack rate is a respectable 13th, so this isn't a pocket-presence collapse; the volume of pressure is the issue. The run game is 29th in EPA, which leaves him in long third downs: 8.3 yards to go on average and a 30.6% conversion rate. Beyond Jaxon Smith-Njigba (0.486 EPA per target), his targets have struggled. AJ Barner and Rashid Shaheed have each been at roughly -0.40 EPA per target on a combined 54 looks. The one clean game proves the point. Against Kansas City he was pressured on 6.7% of dropbacks and added 9.6 EPA.

Not all of it is circumstance. The Chicago game had only modest pressure and still produced a -16.9 CPOE and a 32.4% bad-throw rate. His interception count has ranked near the bottom in most of his seasons. Expect the deep efficiency to cool from an unsustainable level on 20 throws. Expect the short-game CPOE to recover some toward his 2024-25 form. The interceptions will stay a feature, not a bug. The real swing is whether Charles Cross and Quenton Nelson get back on the field.

strengths.title: Downfield throws carry the offense
strengths.body: Everything 10-plus yards out has been strongly positive: high success, above-expected completions and only three picks on 67 such attempts. It comes from a willingness to throw into tight windows and from Smith-Njigba winning outside. The deep number will regress on a 20-attempt sample, but the intermediate game (0.156 EPA on 47 throws) is a sturdier base and matches his last two seasons.

strengths.title: Smith-Njigba connection is real
strengths.body: His top receiver has drawn 68 targets at nearly half a point of EPA each, by far the most productive pairing on the roster. That has held across a rough season, so it is the most bankable thing he has.

strengths.title: Avoids sacks under heavy pressure
strengths.body: Given how often he is pressured, converting only 24.3% of pressures into sacks (13th) is good work. He has also scrambled for six first downs on nine tries. The legs are a small but efficient escape valve, not a volume source.

concerns.title: Short passing has collapsed
concerns.body: Under 10 air yards he is losing points, completing below expectation and throwing interceptions. Screens and throws behind the line alone have cost 16.2 EPA. This is the opposite of his 2025 profile, so it is more likely a product of pressure, scheme and weak secondary targets than a lost skill. Some recovery is reasonable, but not without better protection.

concerns.title: Interceptions in one-score games
concerns.body: Seven of his nine picks and 13 of his 17 sacks came with the game within one score. That is where his EPA has bled out, while his numbers when trailing big are positive. Interceptions have been a career trait, ranking near the bottom in most seasons. A rate this high should ease somewhat, but he will not become careful.

concerns.title: Protection and supporting cast
concerns.body: He has been pressured on nearly a third of dropbacks and Seattle's run game ranks 29th. Barner and Shaheed have been sinks for targets. Both starting tackles and Nelson are on the injury report, so the main cause of his struggles may get worse before it improves.

trend.note: Big swings week to week: +4.3 EPA at Washington, three straight negative games, a +9.6 against Kansas City when kept clean, then -4.5 with poor accuracy against Chicago. His last three games are roughly break-even per dropback, but with a worse CPOE and fewer touchdowns than his season rates.

nextGame.headline: Rematch at San Francisco with a patched line and sore ribs
nextGame.body:
The first meeting was his worst game: 2 interceptions, 5 sacks, 40% pressure and -9.1 EPA. San Francisco's defense profile cuts against his strength. It ranks 4th against deep passes and 6th in explosive passes allowed, which takes away the downfield game carrying him. Its short-pass defense ranks 24th, which invites the quick game, the part of his game that has been broken. The 49ers also own the league's top offense and its run defense ranks 5th. Seattle likely can't lean on its 29th-ranked ground game and may be pulled into a passing race. The saving grace is that San Francisco barely gets home: its sack rate ranks 31st.

Availability is the story. Darnold is listed out with quad and rib injuries, though Macdonald expects him to practice fully out of the bye and start. Cross and Nelson, both near-every-snap starters, are out with an estimated return of game day. Abraham Lucas is questionable with an ankle injury. On the other side, San Francisco has lost interior linemen Gracen Halton and C.J. West to IR, which thins a rush that was already light on sacks. Starting corner Renardo Green is questionable with a back injury and Nate Hobbs is on IR, so the secondary could be short-handed. On offense, Mike Evans' availability shapes how many points Seattle must answer.

keyMatchups.title: Seattle tackles versus a weak rush
keyMatchups.body: If Cross and Lucas can't go, the backups face a front that ranks 31st in sack rate and has lost two interior linemen. That is the most forgiving setup for a patched line. If he gets something like the Kansas City game's clean pocket, his efficiency jumps.

keyMatchups.title: Deep shots into a stingy shell
keyMatchups.body: His best throws are deep, and San Francisco ranks among the hardest teams to hit deep. If Green sits, the deep shots may open up. If not, Darnold needs the quick game to function, and it hasn't all year.

keyMatchups.title: Keeping pace with SF offense
keyMatchups.body: San Francisco's offense leads the league in EPA. A deficit pushes Seattle away from its run-heavy lean. His trailing-big splits are positive, so a chase script could inflate his volume even if efficiency suffers.

nextGame.watch: Whether Cross and Nelson are active and how often Darnold is pressured. In this sample, a clean pocket is the difference between his good and bad games.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect something between this season and last. His short-game accuracy has been far below his 2024-25 standard, and some of that should come back, especially if the line gets healthy. The deep efficiency on 20 attempts will come down, so the net effect is a quarterback near league-average per dropback with more volume than Seattle's run-first lean suggests. That projects to about 205-245 passing yards and 1.1-1.6 touchdowns a game.

The interceptions are the stubborn part. They have followed him across stops, and his aggressiveness is up, so 0.8-1.2 a game is a fair expectation even with improvement. Health is a real wildcard: he returns from quad and rib injuries behind a line missing two starters, and his availability has been spotty all season.
swingFactors: Return of Charles Cross and Quenton Nelson

confidence.note: Seven-game sample with volatile results, an injury return and line uncertainty; the career baseline is clearer than this season.
